item.title: India's diesel export boom set to ease global fuel shortages in 2027
item.description: India is set to boost diesel exports next year as refiners add capacity, potentially easing global supply shortages and strengthening its position in international fuel markets ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Rakesh Sharma A surge in Indian diesel exports is set to hit global markets next year as new refining capacity comes online, bringing much-needed supply to fuel-starved markets from the US to Europe. State-owned refiners will add at least 15 million tons of annual diesel-making capacity through a new refinery and expansions at existing plants, India’s Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Tuesday.  “We’ll be in the happy situation of not only refining for ourselves but for the world,” Puri told reporters on the sidelines of an industry conference in Goa.  The Middle East and Russia-Ukraine wars have disrupted crude and fuel flows, tightening global supplies and driving up prices this year. Diesel has been particularly squeezed after Russia halted exports in July to protect domestic supplies following attacks on its refineries and ports. The crunch sent US diesel prices to a record, prompting Washington to consider export curbs before President Donald Trump struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release more fuel into global markets. The turmoil has created an opportunity for India, already one of the world’s biggest suppliers of diesel, the workhorse fuel that powers farms, factories and heavy transport. The South Asian nation overtook Russia this year to become the world’s second-biggest diesel exporter, according to Kpler data. The refinery expansions could further strengthen India’s global fuel markets share as Goldman Sachs Group Inc. expects supplies to remain tight through 2027. Indian Oil Corp., the country’s largest refiner, expects to produce as much as 9 million tons more diesel annually from next year after completing expansions that will add more than 17 million tons of crude-processing capacity across three refineries, Chairman Arvinder Singh Sahney said. Hindustan Petroleum Corp. will add about 4 million tons of diesel output as its new 9 million-ton-a-year Rajasthan refinery ramps up to full capacity, Chairman Vikas Kaushal said. Oil India Ltd.’s unit Numaligarh Refinery Ltd. will boost production of the fuel to about 3 million tons. Meanwhile, Bharat Petroleum Corp. expects to add 1.5 million tons from 2028, Chairman Sanjay Khanna said. In the first half of the financial year that began in April, Indian refiners produced 59 million tons of the fuel while domestic consumption was about 46 million tons, according to oil ministry data. Overall refining capacity in the country is set to climb to 300 million tons a year from about 267 million tons currently, before reaching 400 million tons in a few years, Puri said.

item.title: China boycotts Kylian Mbappe after perceived insult to Mao Zedong
item.description: CCTV has reportedly removed advertisements featuring Mbappe, stopped airing soccer matches involving the Frenchman and deleted all posts related to him from its official Weibo account ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: French soccer star Kylian Mbappe is facing mounting backlash in China after comments perceived as insulting Mao Zedong, with state TV blocking his matches, social media freezing his accounts and a slew of companies dropping him as ambassador. CCTV has reportedly removed advertisements featuring Mbappe, stopped airing soccer matches involving the Frenchman and deleted all posts related to him from its official Weibo account. Chinese social media platform Xiaohongshu also froze the footballer’s account after controversy erupted over remarks he made while discussing an internet meme that appeared to depict Mao, modern China’s founding father.  Mbappe’s official accounts on Weibo and Xiaohongshu, which both have around 1 million followers, were marked with notices saying they had been muted for violating regulations.  During a press briefing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said that any words or actions that offend the Chinese people will inevitably encounter widespread opposition from Chinese society. Consumer brands that hired Mbappe as ambassador — Eastroc Beverage Group Co. and China Mengniu Dairy Co. — saw their stock drop. Shares of Eastroc fell as much as 4.1% in Shanghai, while Mengniu was down around 3% in Hong Kong. Both companies said they are severing ties with him.  Swiss sneaker company On Holding AG also deleted all Mbappe-related posts on its Chinese social media account. The sportswear brand did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its plans regarding its recently signed 10-year partnership with the 2018 World Cup winner. In a video, the footballer was asked which internet meme featuring himself had made him laugh the most. He described one involving a video of a man he said he thought was “a Chinese dictator,” with his own face superimposed on the figure. Mbappe said he frequently used the meme with friends while gaming online, but didn’t identify the person in the meme.  Taiwanese media outlet ETtoday reported that the image depicted Mao. Images circulating online also appeared to show Mbappe’s face superimposed on Mao. Neither Eastroc or Mengniu specified what prompted their decisions or referred to Mao in their statements.  Memes about Mbappe being a dictator have circulated at least since the World Cup this summer. It’s a nickname he’s carried for months and people have superimposed his face on several historical figures, often in military garb.  The episode quickly triggered criticism from nationalist users on Chinese social media, with some accusing Mbappe of insulting China and calling for a boycott. Prominent soccer outlet Dongqiudi said it wouldn’t provide a translation of his remarks as they were “hurtful to China and the Chinese people.” It’s not the first time that online controversies over perceived slights have hurt sponsorships and business ties. The National Basketball Association has worked to rebuild its brand in mainland China after a years-long fallout triggered by a social-media post supporting Hong Kong protesters in 2019 from Daryl Morey, then general manager of the Houston Rockets. Foreign companies including Swedish retailer Hennes & Mauritz AB and sportswear giant Nike Inc. have also faced consumer boycotts over comments on Xinjiang.

item.title: JLR begins local production of Defender 110, prices to drop by ₹34 lakh
item.description: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) India on Tuesday said it has commenced production of the Defender 110 at its Pune facility to cater to its local customers, thereby reducing prices by up to Rs 34 lakh for the ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Auto / JLR begins local production of Defender 110, prices to drop by ₹34 lakh

JLR begins local production of Defender 110, prices to drop by ₹34 lakh The company said it expects up to a 20 per cent uptick in sales volumes following the move

In the last three and a half years, the company has sold 9,000 units of the Defender | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 3:50 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) India on Tuesday said it has commenced production of the Defender 110 at its Pune facility to cater to its local customers, thereby reducing prices by up to Rs 34 lakh for the fully loaded top-end version. The company said it expects up to a 20 per cent uptick in sales volumes following the move. With this, India becomes the first market outside Europe for local production of Defender, the company said. Global production, however, will continue at JLR's facility in Nitra, Slovakia, which remains the centre of excellence for Defender and will continue to manufacture global variants including Defender OCTA, Defender 90 and Defender 130, it said.   In the last three and a half years, the company has sold 9,000 units of the Defender. Also Read

"The country has embraced Defender for its capability, versatility and unmistakable character. With more than 9,000 Defenders on Indian roads already, and as our highest-selling model, it has moved beyond an SUV to become a cultural icon," said Rajan Amba, Managing Director, JLR India. "This decision to now manufacture (the vehicle) in Pune reflects the scale of our ambition for India and our confidence in the quality and passion of our team and partners here," he added. Lennard Hoornik, Chief Commercial Officer, JLR, said, "India's appetite for adventure and modern luxury has never been stronger. Localising the Defender is a pivotal step in our 'Reimagine' strategy and reinforces our commitment to delivering the unrivalled breadth of capability to Indian clients."   "Manufacturing the Defender in Pune enables us to respond faster to demand while maintaining the tough, rugged engineering and reductive design that makes Defender an icon across the globe," he added. Defender will be available in the country in both 2.0-litre and 3.0-litre petrol, and 3.0-litre diesel engine variants in the X-Dynamic HSE derivative.

item.content:encoded:
Home / Economy / News / No pressure from US to reduce Russian oil imports, says Hardeep Puri

No pressure from US to reduce Russian oil imports, says Hardeep Puri India's imports of West Asian crude oil surged in September, returning to pre-war levels, while its refiners cut back purchases of Russian oil amid stiff competition from China

Hardeep Puri said West Asia oil supplies have been rising as the region is able to ship out more cargoes

Reuters GOA 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 12:49 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India has faced no pressure from the US to reduce its Russian crude imports, oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Tuesday at an industry event.   "I never felt anything," Puri said when asked if there has been pressure to cut Russian oil imports.   Puri said West Asia oil supplies have been rising as the region is able to ship out more cargoes.   He said India was getting 0.2% of its oil imports from Russia before the Ukraine war, while imports have surged since the war started due to discounts on Russian oil.   India's imports of West Asian crude oil surged in September, returning to pre-war levels, while its refiners cut back purchases of Russian oil amid stiff competition from China, ship-tracking data showed.

The minister said that the purchase of Russian oil is linked to discounts and pricing when compared with other grades. Russian oil imports have been reduced as the refiners are buying more Gulf oil sold at a discount, he added.   "Whatever people say or do, ultimately it is anchored in their self-interest," he said.   The minister also said India is expanding its refining capacity to help meet local demand and export commitments.
